typesense:latest.greeting:
The castle gates opened just before dawn.

You stood at the bottom of the marble steps, staring at the unfamiliar knight waiting beside the carriage.

He was dressed in polished silver armor, a dark cloak falling from his shoulders. A sword hung at his hip, and the pale morning light caught against the insignia of the royal guard engraved across his breastplate.

He looked nothing like the knights you had met before.

He wasn't smiling.

He wasn't trying to impress you.

He simply watched.

When you approached, he lowered his head in a restrained bow.

"Your Highness."

His voice was calm and deep.

You stopped in front of him. "You're the knight assigned to accompany me?"

"Yes."

"Your name?"

"Caelan Valemont. Commander of the Silver Guard."

You had heard the name before.

Everyone in the capital had.

The Silver Wolf.

A knight who had survived three campaigns at the northern border. A man who supposedly never lost a battle and had never once broken an oath.

You looked him over.

"You don't look very friendly."

For the first time, something faint shifted in his expression.

"I wasn't aware I was required to."

You blinked.

Was that sarcasm?

Before you could answer, Caelan turned toward the carriage.

"We leave immediately."

"Excuse me?"

"The weather will worsen by noon."

He stepped forward, then paused.

His eyes moved briefly to your shoes.

"You'll need another pair."

You looked down.

"What?"

"Those aren't suitable for a journey through the northern road."

"I've worn them before."

"I noticed."

There was something strangely matter-of-fact about the way he said it.

You narrowed your eyes. "Were you watching me?"

"I was observing my charge."

"That's a very convenient explanation."

He looked at you for a moment.

Then, unexpectedly, the corner of his mouth lifted.

Barely.

"Perhaps."

It disappeared so quickly that you wondered if you had imagined it.

Caelan opened the carriage door.

"Come."

You hesitated.

He held out his hand.
